## fastfetch

**Your iPhone's specs in the terminal, with the Apple logo next to them.** Install it, open a terminal (NewTerm or SSH) and type `fastfetch`.

- **Shows** your model, iOS version, chip, memory, storage, battery, display, package count, uptime and more.
- **Built for iOS**, not just copied from the Mac: it names your chip (like A13 Bionic), counts your Sileo/Zebra packages and only shows the storage that matters.
- **Fast:** about a tenth of a second.
- **Same fastfetch you know:** themes, presets and your own config all work. Try `fastfetch -c neofetch`.

- **iOS 15 and newer**, rootless (Dopamine and other rootless jailbreaks).
- **Tested** on an **iPhone 11 Pro (A13)** with iOS 18.6.2, an **iPhone 11 Pro Max (A13)** with iOS 16.2 and an **iPhone XR (A12)** with iOS 16.0.3.
- **iOS 15 and 17** aren't tested yet. Please [report back](https://github.com/Jond-ie/repo/issues).

- It's a command, not a tweak: nothing runs in the background and no respring is needed.
- Some parts of fastfetch only exist on computers (Wi-Fi name, Bluetooth, fonts, wallpaper), so those lines stay hidden on iPhone.
- Already have another fastfetch installed? This one replaces it.

**[fastfetch](https://github.com/fastfetch-cli/fastfetch)** is made by the fastfetch-cli team (MIT license). Ported to iOS by **Jond-ie**, after the request in [fastfetch issue #2076](https://github.com/fastfetch-cli/fastfetch/issues/2076).
